about: The priest offers the host to God the Father for his own sins, offenses, and negligences, for all who are present, and for all faithful Christians, living and dead. In this prayer the priest asks that the offering may bring salvation and eternal life both to him and to them.

seg.nr: At solemn Mass the deacon hands the celebrant the paten with the Host. Otherwise the priest takes it himself and offers it while saying the prayer.

seg.tr: Receive, holy Father, almighty eternal God, this spotless host, which I, Your unworthy servant, offer to You, my God, living and true, for my countless sins and offenses and negligences, and for all those present here, and also for all faithful Christians, living and dead, that it may avail me and them for salvation unto eternal life. Amen.

a.g: my countless sins, offenses, and negligences

ex.w021: The phrase “Deo vivo et vero” also occurs in 1 Thessalonians 1:9.
